title: The Kharijites
hook: a group rejects the arbitration, declares others unbelievers, and fights Ali

segments.voice: Yesterday, Siffin: the fighting stopped and two judges were chosen. Your line was pages on the spears. Did you catch a text being used to win rather than to agree? Day eight hundred eighty-four.

No judgment but God's. In Arabic, la hukma illa lillah. On their face, those are words nobody in Ali's camp would argue with. But a group of his own soldiers begins shouting them at him. They say: you let men judge between you and Mu'awiyah, and judgment belongs to God alone. Some of them, the histories note, were among those who had pushed him to accept the talks in the first place. Now they walk out of his camp and set up their own. Today's word is the name the walkout earned them.
screen: `NO JUDGMENT BUT GOD'S.` → `SHOUTED AT ALI.` → `THEY WALK OUT.`

segments.voice: Kharijites, in Arabic khawarij: those who went out. Ali's answer to their slogan is kept in Sahih Muslim: a word of truth, by which falsehood is intended. The words were true. What they were being used for was not. And what were they used for? The Kharijites came to hold that anyone who accepted the arbitration had committed a grave sin, and that such a person was no longer a believer. Ali, they said, had left Islam. So had anyone who stood with him. Once you've declared someone an unbeliever, the histories show how quickly the next step comes. Reports say they killed Muslims on the road who would not condemn Ali. Ali first sent his cousin Ibn Abbas to reason with them, and the reports say some came back. The rest he fought at Nahrawan. The Prophet had warned about this move long before. Bukhari records him saying that if a person calls his brother an unbeliever, the word returns to one of the two of them. In other words, the charge is dangerous enough that it can land on the one who makes it. Bukhari and Muslim also report the Prophet describing people who would recite the Qur'an but whose recitation would not go past their throats, and Muslim's collection sets that warning beside Ali and the men he faced. A note of fairness: Ibadi Muslims, in Oman and elsewhere, trace part of their history to early dissenters of this time, but they reject the name Kharijite and the extremes it stands for. The lesson the tradition draws is about a single move: declaring. Your line: not our place to declare.
screen: `KHAWARIJ: THOSE WHO WENT OUT.` · `A WORD OF TRUTH, FOR FALSEHOOD.` · `THE WORD RETURNS TO ONE OF THE TWO.` · `IBADIS REJECT THE NAME.` · then, large: `NOT OUR PLACE TO DECLARE.`

segments.voice: The practice: notice the danger of calling others unbelievers, or anything like it. Settle, and breathe. Think of the labels you reach for to put someone outside: fake, sellout, not a real one, not one of us. Breathe in, and find one person you've quietly placed outside the circle. Breathe out, and hand the verdict back. You can still disagree with them completely. You just don't sign the declaration. If you pray, you can leave the judgment with God. The bell holds the time.
The Kharijites. Those who went out: soldiers who left Ali over the arbitration, declared other Muslims unbelievers, and fought him at Nahrawan. Today's word.
Your line: not our place to declare. Today, when you hear yourself about to say someone isn't a real anything, stop at the label and talk about the action instead. Day eight hundred eighty-four.

howItsDone: Muslim teachers often use the Kharijites as a warning against takfir, declaring other Muslims unbelievers, and cite the hadith that the charge returns to one of the two.

myth: Ali called it a word of truth, used for a falsehood.
calling a fellow Muslim an unbeliever can rebound on the speaker
Bukhari records the Prophet saying the word returns to one of the two.
they trace part of their history to early dissenters but reject the name.

fork.setup: you're Ali. a group of your own men has walked out, shouting that you've left Islam. what do you do first?
options: send Ibn Abbas to reason with them.
fork.reveal: the reports say he sent Ibn Abbas first, and some came back; he fought the rest at Nahrawan.

original.note: Arabic: those who went out, the name given to the group that left Ali's camp.

trapdoor: what you thought: the Kharijites were just rebels.
what it means: soldiers who left Ali over the arbitration and declared other Muslims unbelievers.
what a scholar hears: Ali's 'word of truth, by which falsehood is intended' in Sahih Muslim, the hadith that the charge of unbelief returns to one of the two, and the long warning against takfir.
recall: the one who stands in front
